page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Running head and page number at the top. Marginal notes in the left margin: a Scripture reference beside the first paragraph, a note on "necessitas", and a reference beside the Epictetus quotation.

main_text.p: non effet gens humana ignorantiæ & perfidiæ heu nimis obnoxium: quo fortasse spectant illa Christi verba {a}ἐκ τῶ πνευμάτος ἔστιν[?]Math. 5. 37. Ergo ficut vitandus est medicinæ usus, ubi ad vitæ conservationem & valetudinem tuendam non videtur esse quodammodo necessaria: sic & Juramentum vitandum, ubi conservandæ humanæ societatis {o}necessitas, veritatis manifestatio, & fidei confirmatio, non videntur ipsius usum aliquo modo effla-gitare.In totum jurare, nisi ubi necesse est, gravi viro parum convenit. Salutare monitum est illud Epicteti(ut illius Stoici omnia) Quintil. 9 inst. 2. in Enchirid.ὅρκον πάντως, εἰ δὲ μή[?], ὡς ἐπὶ τὸ πολὺ[?], ἐν τῶν ἐνόντων[?]. Jusjurandum devita, si possibile est, omnino: si non, saltem quantum potes. Sancta res est Juramentum: sed quo sanctior, eo periculosior, si indebite adhibeatur. Sicut pharmacum, quo majoris est efficaciæ & virtutis, eo magis corpori nocet, si temere & imperite sumatur. Juramenti assertorii in Rep. ne-cessarius usus est: in publicis præsertim judiciis, ad veritatem eruendam circa facta particularia; quo pertinent jura-menta testium, calumniæ, purgationis, &c.
Extra judicium & in rebus privatis usus ejus rarior est: potest tamen quandoque esse necessarius; ubi sc. multum in-tereft,

page.notes: The Greek lines are partly uncertain and marked [?]; the Epictetus Greek in particular is read with doubt. The Scripture Greek after {a} is also doubtful. The phrase "ad .veritatem" has a stray dot before "veritatem" as printed, which is left in the text as a possible printing error. Large section of the Greek on the first line is read from a small scan.
